summary: Enterprise Suite AC-11 in-memory Workflow dispatch queue reference adapter records cross-product Workflow dispatch intents with idempotency validation and duplicate-dispatch refusal while explicitly avoiding live Workflow execution, broker, and durable queue claims.

findings: The adapter is a small BTreeMap/BTreeSet reference queue with no broker/provider configuration or hidden I/O.
Duplicate dispatch keys and malformed keys fail deterministically.
Separates Workflow dispatch seam behavior from engine/broker/cloud wiring, matching repo port/adapter patterns.
Capability flags keep durable queue, Workflow engine, broker publish, runtime execution, child-service calls, and audit-chain emission false until real adapters land.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: duplicate dispatch and malformed key tests
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if duplicate dispatches are accepted, malformed keys reserve, or capability flags imply live Workflow/broker/runtime execution.
findings: Positive queueing of Workflow dispatch metadata and negative duplicate/key-shape tests are covered.
The crate exposes a named dispatch port trait, in-memory queue, dispatch record shape, and capability descriptor.
Workflow adapter tests, suite package-group tests/clippy, 18-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

alternatives_named: add an in-memory Workflow dispatch seam reference first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: In-memory reference pins dispatch record and idempotency contracts without overclaiming live Workflow execution or broker/cloud integration.
rejected_reasons: Workflow engine wiring requires auth, retry, durable queue, execution, observability, and SLO evidence not present in this slice.
Broker publish would introduce runtime I/O and operational claims before cloud integration evidence exists.

findings: No secrets/provider credentials are introduced.
Idempotency key validation rejects empty, whitespace, path traversal, and duplicate keys.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No live Workflow execution exists; tests exercise fixed-size in-memory dispatch records.

findings.summary: Operations are bounded by BTreeMap/BTreeSet key operations over in-process metadata; no network, filesystem, broker, database, or Workflow engine I/O is introduced.

findings: Dispatch-record and capability public fields carry data_class annotations.
Capability response explicitly marks durable queue, Workflow engine, broker publish, runtime execution, child-service calls, and audit-chain emission false.
The change is additive: one in-memory workflow adapter crate, catalog row, workspace membership, spec/tasks/evidence updates, and no migrations or external resources.

Queued dispatch records carry topic, workflow ref, object-graph relationship ref, gate counts, evidence counts, AI suggestion ref, idempotency key, schema version, and backend label for future telemetry labels.
Enterprise Suite AC-11 and D-08 record the Workflow dispatch seam while live Workflow engine, durable queue, broker, runtime execution, child-service calls, and SLO evidence remain future slices.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A Workflow dispatch seam reference can land before live Workflow execution if it is explicitly volatile and capability flags keep all engine/broker/runtime claims false.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/enterprise-suite.json AC-11 and workflow queue capability tests
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Future Workflow engine/broker adapters would lack a tested idempotency and dispatch record-shape contract for suite cross-product workflows.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Shared Workflow products exist, but this missing seam is Enterprise Suite dispatch-adapter behavior rather than engine execution.

findings: This advances Enterprise Suite toward later cloud Workflow integration without pretending live dispatch/execution exists.
Names follow Enterprise Suite Workflow dispatch, in-memory, idempotency, queue, and metadata record vocabulary.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, todo, evidence, catalog, and audit-chain references were updated.
Workflow-dispatch-specific code lives in a new Enterprise Suite adapter crate; runtime/API/app/domain behavior remains unchanged.
No Workflow engine client, broker SDK, database migration, provider SDK, runtime execution integration, child-service client, cloud adapter, or audit emitter was introduced.
No new third-party dependencies were added; the crate depends only on existing Enterprise Suite app crate.
Dispatch records include schema_version and stable topic/idempotency fields; no wire API schema is changed.
Queue helpers deterministically map existing app envelopes into dispatch record views and then enforce key validation/duplicate checks before insert.
